name: Adi Parva
description: Introduces the genealogy of the Bharata dynasty, the births of the Pandavas and Kauravas, the early rivalries, and the burning of the lac palace.

name: Sabha Parva
englishMeaning: The Book of the Assembly Hall
description: Details the construction of the Maya Sabha, the Rajasuya sacrifice of Yudhishthira, the fatal game of dice, the humiliation of Draupadi, and the exile of the Pandavas.

name: Vana Parva
englishMeaning: The Book of the Forest (Aranya Parva)
description: Chronicles the twelve years of forest exile of the Pandavas, containing philosophical dialogues, pilgrimages, the Yaksha Prashna, and the story of Savitri and Nala.

name: Virata Parva
description: The thirteenth year of exile spent in disguise at the court of King Virata. The Pandavas navigate hidden identities, dignity in servitude, and the defense of the kingdom.

name: Udyoga Parva
description: Preparations for war after the failed return of the kingdom. Krishna undertakes the peace embassy to Hastinapura, trying to prevent war, and has a secret, poignant dialogue with Karna.

name: Bhishma Parva
description: The commencement of the Kurukshetra war. Contains the Bhagavad Gita as Krishna instructs Arjuna, and concludes with Bhishma falling upon the bed of arrows.

name: Drona Parva
description: Drona takes command of the Kaurava forces. Features the tragic death of young Abhimanyu in the Chakravyuha, intense sorrow, and Drona's demise.

name: Karna Parva
description: Karna assumes leadership of the Kaurava army. Details the climactic duel between Arjuna and Karna, exploring destiny, vows, social rejection, and ultimate sacrifice.

name: Shalya Parva
description: The final day of open battle. Shalya's brief command, the mace duel between Bhima and Duryodhana at Samantapanchaka, and the collapse of the Kauravas.

name: Sauptika Parva
englishMeaning: The Book of the Sleeping Warriors
description: Ashwatthama, consumed by grief and fury over his father's death, unleashes a midnight raid on the sleeping Pandava camp, slaughtering the remaining warriors and children.

name: Stri Parva
description: The women of both sides grieve upon the devastated battlefield. Queen Gandhari confronts Krishna with immense grief and places a curse upon the Yadava clan.

name: Shanti Parva
description: The longest book of the epic. Yudhishthira, traumatized by the war's slaughter, seeks to renounce the throne. Krishna brings him to the dying Bhishma for exhaustive teachings on statecraft, ethics, and liberation.

name: Anushasana Parva
description: Continuation of Bhishma's discourses on duty, charity, the sanctity of life, the Vishnu Sahasranama, and the moment of Bhishma's willing departure (Iccha Mrityu).

name: Ashvamedhika Parva
englishMeaning: The Book of the Horse Sacrifice
description: The performance of the Ashvamedha sacrifice by Yudhishthira to heal the realm. Contains the Anugita, where Krishna reiterates philosophical truths to Arjuna.

name: Ashramavasika Parva
description: Dhritarashtra, Gandhari, Kunti, and Vidura renounce palace life to retire to the forest as ascetics, eventually perishing peacefully in a forest fire.

name: Mausala Parva
description: The self-destruction of the Vrishni/Yadava dynasty through infighting, fulfilling Gandhari's curse, followed by Krishna's quiet departure from the earthly realm.

name: Mahaprasthanika Parva
englishMeaning: The Book of the Great Journey
description: The Pandavas and Draupadi renounce their kingdom to walk towards the Himalayas. One by one they fall due to subtle personal flaws, leaving Yudhishthira accompanied only by a faithful dog.

name: Svargarohana Parva
englishMeaning: The Book of the Ascent to Heaven
description: Yudhishthira's final test in the afterlife, the unveiling of Maya, the reconciliation of all warriors, and the ultimate transcendence beyond hatred and rivalry.
